prompt:
From the user’s note, normalize only the single block of contact label/value lines (labels may vary; separators include colon, equals and tab). Return only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or null.

Trim and collapse whitespace. Absent, empty or case-insensitive placeholder values (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD) are null. Do not infer from notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes. The only missing-value exception is country from an international phone as described below.

Assign @ values to email and phone-like values to phone regardless of their labels. For phone recognition, strip leading tel: and trailing extensions (ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by digits); require at least seven digits and only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . /. Swap name and company if the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not.

• Name: reorder Last, First at the first comma, remove leading Dr/Mr/Mrs/Ms/Mx/Prof (any case, optional dot), and uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics without transliteration.
• Company: strip a trailing legal suffix and optional preceding comma, ignoring case; uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Legal suffixes: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.
• Email: strip surrounding < > and mailto: prefix, then lowercase the entire address.
• Country: normalize the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish or German names, alpha-2/alpha-3 codes and common aliases, case-insensitively: UK/Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA/U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.
• Phone: output E.164 (+ and digits only), without tel: or extension. After ignoring a leading opening parenthesis, + and 00 mark international numbers. Remove international (0), strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and convert initial 00 to +. Preserve the written calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. If the country is missing, derive it only from a calling code belonging to one country; shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave it null. For national numbers, strip separators, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country’s calling code; without a country, return null for phone.

Worked example input:
Please file this before the next handoff.
Name = VELQUORIN FABLEWORKS, ApS
Org: ŠEVRÅN, mX. ÉLVI-NØR
E-mail: tel: (0045) 73/64.28-19 #57
Tel: <mailto:ELVI@VELQUORIN.INVALID>
Land: TBD
Leave the ticket open for review.

Worked example output:
{"name":"Élvi-Nør Ševrån","phone":"+4573642819","email":"elvi@velquorin.invalid","company":"Velquorin Fableworks","country":"DK"}
